title: Printable statements card sort
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 2: Number sense; sets and probability; primes and proof
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 84 (Printable statements card sort)
intro: Lesson 84: Proof by counterexample and year review. To understand how one counterexample disproves a general statement, and how to review a year of learning

cards: The sum of two odd numbers is even.
A square number has an odd number of factors.
The product of two negative numbers is negative.
A multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3.
blocks.task: sort into always, sometimes and never true.
blocks.answer: Always: sum of two odd numbers is even; a square number has an odd number of factors; a multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3. Sometimes: a prime is odd (not 2); multiplying makes bigger (not by numbers below 1). Never: two negatives multiply to a negative.

cards: the sum of two odd numbers is even
a multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3
blocks.title: Sort into: True / False
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: True, False.
blocks.answer: True: the sum of two odd numbers is even; a multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3. False: squaring makes a number bigger; all primes are odd

questions.q: Find a counterexample: 'the difference of two primes is always even'.
questions.model: 2 is the only even prime, so use it. 5 - 2 = 3, which is odd.

questions.q: True or false: 'a number with 3 factors is a square'?
questions.a: True (it is the square of a prime)

questions.q: Decide true or false and give a counterexample or a reason: (a) all even numbers are multiples of 4 (b) the product of two odd numbers is odd (c) a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides is a square (d) n² ≥ n for every whole number n
questions.a: (a) false: 6 (b) true: (2a + 1)(2b + 1) = 2(2ab + a + b) + 1 (c) false: a rhombus (d) true for whole numbers (0 and 1 are equal; others bigger)
questions.model: (a) Try 6: even but 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5: counterexample. (c) A rhombus has 4 equal sides but no right angles.

questions.q: Show that n² + n + 41 is not prime when n = 41.
